name: TrivyScan
description: Run Trivy from a curated docker runner image and gate the build on findings.
author: iksoftware
helpMarkDown: See the project README for configuration.

inputs.name: target
inputs.label: Target
inputs.helpMarkDown: Image reference for an image scan, otherwise a path relative to the sources directory.

inputs.name: runner
inputs.label: Runner alias
inputs.helpMarkDown: Alias from Collection Settings > Trivy Scanner. Leave empty to use the default runner.

inputs.name: ignoreFile
inputs.label: Ignore file
inputs.helpMarkDown: Path to a .trivyignore file, relative to the sources directory (not an absolute path). Example: `.trivyignore` or `config/.trivyignore`.

inputs.name: publishTestResults
inputs.label: Publish findings as test results
inputs.helpMarkDown: Publishes every finding as a JUnit test case via `results.publish`, giving each one its own row in the Tests tab with history (Failing since, New vs. Existing) and filtering, for free. Off by default: turning this on makes every finding a *failed* test, so a build whose gate passes (failOn not tripped, or the gate disabled) would suddenly show failing tests in the Tests tab. That is exactly the point for a team that wants per-finding history there, but it is a surprise for everyone else, so it is opt-in rather than on by default. See the README section on publishing test results.

inputs.name: targetRegistryConnection
inputs.label: Registry connection for the scanned image

inputs.name: configConnection
inputs.label: Settings connection (PAT)
inputs.helpMarkDown: Only needed when the job cannot read extension settings with its OAuth token.

inputs.name: sourceTransfer
inputs.label: Source transfer
inputs.helpMarkDown: How the sources reach the scan container. Leave as Mount unless this agent's docker daemon cannot see the agent's own filesystem (e.g. a Kubernetes agent reached through a mounted host docker socket) -- see the README section on running the agent in a container.

options.mount: Mount (default; requires a shared filesystem with the docker daemon)
options.copy: Copy (docker cp; no shared filesystem needed, but slower and skips the local database cache)

inputs.name: workingDirectory
inputs.label: Working directory
inputs.helpMarkDown: Directory to scan from, relative to the sources directory (not an absolute path). Example: `services/api`.
